description:
[Servers] Is this server vanilla? Status, differences, claims and published settings. The "Is this server vanilla?" card from the server's page, built from what the server itself publishes (its
Steam tags and A2S rules) compared with Rust's own defaults: `status` (`vanilla` = no modded tag, `modded` =
tagged modded, which puts it in the in-game browser's Modded tab, `unknown` = tags not read yet), `label`
(e.g. "Vanilla · Oxide"), `framework` (oxide/carbon when installed), `summary` (one paragraph), `differences`
(settings that differ from the defaults: game mode, PvE, team size, hidden map, custom map, premium, plugin tags
- each with `value`, `default`, `source` tags/rules and a `note`), `evidence` (positive signs: no modded tag,
unmodified game code checksum), `claims` (what the NAME or owner tags claim - "2x", "vanilla", "no decay" -
with `conflict` true when the settings contradict it), `choices` (map size), `not_checkable` (settings servers
never publish, e.g. gather rate, decay, upkeep - nobody outside can verify them), plus `published` (game mode,
PvE, custom map, connect address, game build, website/Discord/socials, logo and banner, description) and the
server's `brand` (network) when it has one. Cached for five minutes. Use for 'is <server> vanilla / modded / really 2x?': what the server itself publishes vs Rust's defaults, and where its name or tags claim something the settings contradict. Gather rates, decay and upkeep are never published (not_checkable) - say so
name: check_server_vanilla
title: Is this server vanilla? Status, differences, claims and published settings
